samples.summary: `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` is the one XML-attribute lookup in the hardening pass that stayed an object literal with an untrusted key — and the comment added right above it asserts the opposite
samples.evidence: This PR converted DASH_VAL, ALGN, UNDERLINE_STYLE_TO_U, KIND_TO_OOXML, SIZE_TO_OOXML, ROUTING_PRST, BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE, TYPE_TO_TAG, DIR_TO_ATTR, EFFECT_TO_PRESET, START_TO_NODE_TYPE and DOCX_ALIGNMENTS to `Map`s precisely because an object lookup consults the prototype chain. `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:48-50) still does `const val = ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` and interpolates `val` into `<a:schemeClr val="...">` with no fallback. `c.role` is untrusted: `colorChildXml` is called from `solidFillXml`/`fillXml`/`gradFillXml`, which receive `ThemeColor`s straight off persisted element JSON — `shapeToXml` -> `fillXml(data.fill)` (shape.ts:188), `lineXml` -> `colorFromStringOrTheme(stroke.color)` (shape.ts:150), `tcPrXml` cell fill/border (table.ts:118,128), `effectsToXml` shadow color (effects.ts:19) — and the new backend validator walks only element *text bodies*, never `data.fill` / `data.stroke` / `data.effects`. So a workspace member (or an API-key caller through PUT /content) can persist `{"kind":"role","role":"constructor"}` and the exporter emits `<a:schemeClr val="function Object() { [native code] }"/>`, or `val="undefined"` for any unknown own key — a corrupt .pptx. I could NOT complete an injection chain: no `Object.prototype` member stringifies to anything containing `"`, so the attribute cannot be closed today; the exposure is a schema-invalid export plus a latent injection if any prototype-pollution gadget ever lands in the same process. The added comment at lines 29-31 ("every attribute this function emits is either `[0-9A-F]{6}`, a closed `ROLE_TO_SCHEME` value, or a finite number") and at line 58 ("matching the 'unknown role' fallback below") both claim a closure/fallback that does not exist in this function — `text.ts:212` validates roles against `Object.keys(ROLE_TO_SCHEME)` before calling, but none of the other callers do.

samples.summary: The slides PUT validator walks only text bodies, so every other persisted-verbatim deck field (element fills/strokes/effects, themes[], masters[]) still reaches the OOXML sinks unvalidated
searchedFor: read packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts in full (assertValidSlidesBody, assertValidLayout, assertValidSlide, assertValidElement, assertValidElementData, assertValidTextBodyBlocks, assertValidSlideBlocks, normalizeSlideInlines)
grep 'writeSlidesRoot|writeDocsRoot|writeNoteRoot' across packages/backend/src for other write paths (only document-copy.service.ts, which copies already-normalized content)
grep 'TextBody|Block\[\]|blocks:' in packages/slides/src/model to enumerate every element arm holding docs Blocks
grep '=\"\$\{' across packages/slides/src/export to enumerate every attribute sink
read color.ts, theme.ts, table.ts, shape.ts, layout.ts, animation.ts, effects.ts, image.ts, text.ts, xml.ts
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` (line 612) only recurses into `data.blocks` / `data.text` / `data.rows[].cells[].body` / `data.children`; `assertValidSlidesBody` (line 472) checks `themes`/`masters`/`layouts`/`slides` are arrays and never looks inside `themes[i]` or `masters[i]`. So an authenticated caller can PUT a deck whose `elements[].data.fill.color` is `{"kind":"role","role":"constructor"}` (feeds the unclosed lookup in finding 1) or whose `themes[i]` omits `colors` entirely — `themeToXml` does `theme.colors[role]` unconditionally (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:97), a TypeError that aborts export for *every* collaborator on that deck, which is exactly the 'crashing shape for every viewer' the diff's own `normalizeSlideInlines` docblock says must not be persistable. Note the endpoint is not the only writer — browser collaborators write the Yorkie doc directly — so the sinks, not this validator, are the real boundary; that is why I rate impact low. But rest-api.md as amended advertises 'the same block-style value checks are applied to the docs Blocks wherever a deck stores them', which reads as broader coverage than exists.

finding.summary: OOXML attribute injection sink left unsealed by the sweep: `anim.durationMs` / `anim.delayMs` / `anim.pptxPreset.id` are interpolated raw into `<p:cTn dur=…>`, `presetID=` and `<p:cond delay=>`
finding.evidence: Attack: a caller with write access to a deck PUTs `slides[0].animations = [{ elementId: <an id that exists on the slide>, start: 'onClick', category: 'entrance', effect: 'fadeIn', durationMs: "500\"><p:evil/><p:cTn id=\"0\" dur=\"1" }]`. The backend never validates `slide.animations` — `assertValidSlide` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:518-558) checks only id/layoutId/background/elements/notes — and `writeSlidesRoot` stores the slide object verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:105). No read-side codec normalizes it (grep for `durationMs` in packages/slides/src finds no migration). On PPTX export, `slideToXml` calls `animationsToTimingXml(slide.animations ?? [], spidMap)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:163) and `effectParXml` emits `` `<p:cTn id="0" dur="${anim.durationMs}" …` `` (animation.ts:221), `` presetID="${presetID}" `` (line 222, where presetID = the persisted `pptxPreset.id`) and `` delay="${anim.delayMs ?? 0}" `` (line 223) with no coercion and no escaping — unlike the sibling values `presetClass`/`presetSubtype` on the same lines, which ARE run through `escapeXmlAttr`. The string closes the attribute and injects attacker-chosen elements/attributes into ppt/slides/slideN.xml of any .pptx a victim later exports (`renumberCTnIds` is a plain regex and does not sanitize). Every other numeric sink in the exporters is safe because it passes through `Math.round`/`pxToEmu*` (NaN, not a string) — these three are the exception.

verdict.reason: The claimed raw interpolation does not exist in the working tree. All three flagged attributes are coerced through `toXmlInt` (animation.ts:82-85), which returns `String(Math.round(Number(value)))` only when the value is a finite number and otherwise returns a numeric fallback — so no attacker-controlled string can reach the XML. Concretely: `dur="${toXmlInt(anim.durationMs, 500)}"` (line 256), `delay="${toXmlInt(anim.delayMs ?? 0, 0)}"` (line 258), and `presetID` assigned via `toXmlInt(anim.pptxPreset.id, 1)` (line 218) / `toXmlInt(preset?.id, 1)` (line 224) before interpolation at line 257. `presetSubtype` is likewise coerced (line 233). The cited lines 221-223 are the EFFECT_TO_PRESET lookup and presetClass fallback, not an emit site. The claimed payload `500"><p:evil/>...` yields NaN and emits the fallback `500`. Remaining values in the same template are already escaped or come from closed Maps: `presetClass` and `motionPath` via `escapeXmlAttr` (lines 245, 257; xml.ts:5-12), `nodeType` via START_TO_NODE_TYPE with `?? 'clickEffect'` (line 208), and `spid` is an integer from the id→spid map with unmapped elements skipped (lines 321-322). A grep over packages/slides/src/export confirms no other emitter of these fields exists.
